content:
maya: quick thread — p99 in us-west spiked from 220ms -> 820ms after we enabled cross-zone fallback for region routing at 15:02 UTC :grimacing:
liam: saw that too, correlates with a KV cache miss surge and a routing fanout to ap-southeast, which adds serialization and kernel warmups
sophia: uploading short profile and KV miss breakdown (flamegraph + timeline) :point_down:
perf-bot: profiling run #482 complete — flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/482 :white_check_mark:
noah: key observations from the profile:
- bulk of added latency is in RPC fanout and model kernel init on fallback shards
- microbatch size jumps from 4->16 when fallback occurs because of pooling heuristic
- KV cache eviction rate increased 3.8x during the spike
liam: the microbatch jump is the kicker — our batching heuristic uses region-local queue length + global autoscaler hint. On fallback we accidentally treat cross-region queues as "cold" and wait longer to fill a batch
maya: here's the minimal repro (ran in staging) — p99 before fallback: 210ms, after fallback: 760ms
```
# simplified loadgen commands
loadgen --region us-west --qps 120 --seq-len 128 --microbatch-target 4
# trigger routing fallback in policy
curl -XPOST https://routing/redwood/force_fallback -d '{"region":"us-west","fallback":"ap-southeast"}'
```
noah: also noticed kernel selection flip from int8-optimized path to FP16 path on fallback nodes (different CUDA kernels), adds ~60-90ms per token for short sequences
sophia: KV cache behavior: when fallback fanout occurs, prefix locality breaks and miss amplification causes extra KV RPCs which block request path pre-batching. TTLs are fine, it's locality not staleness
liam: short-term mitigation options:
- clamp microbatch max to 8 for cross-region fallback cases (reduces wait time)
- change routing policy to prefer local degraded nodes over full fanout unless capacity < 20%
- warm up kernel (async warmup) on fallback target when routing decision predicts fanout
maya: medium-term: adjust batching heuristic to use per-region warmness score and KV hit-rate as inputs, not queue length alone. That should avoid the 4->16 jump
sophia: quick patch uploaded: reduced fallback microbatch cap + add KV-hit-rate check in heuristic. PR: https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/789 :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for eng-runtime/fallback-batching-patch -> canary group 2 (us-west small) :shipit:
perf-bot: quick telemetry after canary (1 min window): p95 improved 15%, p99 reduced from 820ms -> 360ms, KV miss-rate down 45% :tada:
liam: still want to experiment with async kernel warmup + kernel hint in routing response. If we can preselect compatible kernel variants before final routing we'll shave extra cold-start millis
maya: agree. Follow-ups:
- sophia to land heuristic + cap (in progress)
- noah to prototype async kernel-warmup flow (esp for cross-zone targets)
- liam to run A/B with warmness score threshold adjustments and report p95/p99 tradeoffs
- ops to monitor long-tail (>1s) errors during rollout :eyes:
noah: one extra note — longer sequences (>=512) don't see as bad p99 delta since batching dominates token time; short chats (<=128) are most affected
sophia: adding a small dashboard tile for 'fallback-induced microbatch size' and 'kv-miss amplification' so we can catch this earlier :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maya: thanks all. if canary stays green we'll push full rollout tomorrow morning PST. tagging @eng-sre for post-rollout watch
